message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to individual university timetables, but I can share what’s typically true for the main campuses in Sydney as of my last update (mid‑2024).

| Institution | Typical Term 1 Dates* | Notes |
|-------------|-----------------------|-------|
| **University of New South Wales** (UNSW) | Mid‑Feb – End‑June (≈ 19–21 weeks) | Most undergraduate & postgraduate courses begin in week 2–5. Enrolments close around mid‑April for the current academic year. |
| **University of Technology Sydney** (UTS) | Early Feb – Late Jun (≈ 18–20 weeks) | Similar structure to UNSW. Short “short‑course” modules sometimes offered later in the term. |
| **Macquarie University** | Early Feb – Late Jun (≈ 18 weeks) | Courses often start in week 3–7. |
| **Western Sydney University** | Early Feb – Late Jun (≈ 17–19 weeks) | Same pattern. |
| **Australian Catholic University – Sydney Campus** | Early Feb – Late Jun (≈ 18 weeks) | |

\*These dates reflect the standard calendar used for the 2024 Academic Year. Exact start/end days vary slightly each year.

### What this means for May
- **May falls squarely inside Semester 1**, so almost all regular degree programmes will still be running.  
- If you’re looking for *new* enrollments in May itself, it depends on whether the institution offers:
  - **Short‑term workshops / intensive courses** that launch after the first few weeks of the semester.
  - **Summer school programs** (often held in July/August rather than May).
- For most full‑credit courses, registration closes well before May—usually sometime between March and April—so new students generally join either at the beginning of the semester (late Jan/early Feb) or via special entry pathways (e.g., bridging courses, part‑time study starting later).

### How to find out exactly
Because schedules change yearly and different faculties may set their own timelines, here are practical steps:

1. **Visit the official website of the university/faculty** you’re interested in. Look under sections titled “Academic Calendar,” “Course Catalogue,” or “Student Services.”  
   - Example URLs (replace `university.edu.au` with the actual domain):
     ```
     https://www.university.edu.au/calendar/
     https://www.university.edu.au/course-catalogue/
     ```

2. **Check the enrolment portal** (many universities host a student self‑service system where you can view upcoming semesters and register).  

3. **Contact the Registrar’s Office or Student Support Centre** directly via email or phone. A quick inquiry such as:
   > “Hello, could you let me know when the next cohort starts for [specific program] and whether there are any openings in May?”  
   Usually replies come within one business day.

4. **Look for “summer schools” or “intensive courses” listings**. These are often advertised separately and may commence in May or even later in the year.

---

#### Bottom line
While May is definitely within the active teaching period for most universities in Sydney, enrolling into a brand‑new class during that month isn’t common because registrations normally finish months earlier. To get definitive confirmation, reach out to the particular campus or faculty you’re targeting—they’ll tell you exact opening dates, application windows, and whether any May‑start options exist.
